comparator.name: Bachelor Automotive Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official after-revision EE/AT curriculum for 2026–2027, latest version 2 July 2026, was freshly retrieved and visually inspected on 8 October 2026. Only common and AT rows form this Automotive Technology reconstruction; EE-only rows are alternatives and are not stacked into the degree. Current core totals 125 EC, including 5XEC0 Final Bachelor Project 10, with ITEC Ethics 0LVX30 5 and ITEC Society 0LVX40 5 (10 total) and genuine free elective space 45. This replaces the older 120-core/15-USE-ITEC/45 allocation. Year one is 60 core EC; year two is 40 core + 5 ITEC + 15 free; year three is 25 core including project + 5 ITEC + 30 free. All 27 course/project/open-space positions total 180. Current 4AUB10 is Propulsion Systems, and is not relabelled as the older Electric and Hybrid Propulsion Systems. DBL Autonomous Vehicles Conquering the World 5AID0, DBL Automotive Design Project Electronic Differential 5XSC0 and Semiconductor Technology 5XPG0 appear among optional courses, not universal compulsory core; they are not added as required formation. Open electives retain university approval, overlap and applicable level conditions; no example optional course is forced into the free space. The curriculum table establishes required membership and credits, not a guarantee of exact future timetable or individual course admission. The project row uses ambiguous quarter/timeslot notation; no exact scheduling claim is inferred from it.

core: Mathematics, signals, optimisation and system models
Programming, algorithms, perception and autonomous decision systems
Integrated product design and complex-system decisions
adjacent: Sustainable energy, lifecycle and resource systems for mobility

examines interpretability, bias, alignment and responsibility in AI systems used for autonomous decisions; it is not the full external technology-and-society sequence

provides data cleaning, visualisation and spatial-data analysis for mobility and sensor datasets
applies regression, tree-based and other machine-learning methods to real data
directly studies image feature detection and tracking with documented self-driving, robotics and traffic-management applications
develops neural networks for computer vision and other perception tasks
studies kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and robotic manipulation as general computational autonomy rather than automotive hardware

develops vector spaces, matrices, transformations and eigenvalue methods

alternatives.label: Autonomous systems, sensing & connected mobility
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical system models with programming, algorithms, computer vision, robotics, machine learning, networks, product design and lifecycle assessment to study sensing, autonomous decisions and connected mobility. This is a computational systems response, not a vehicle-engineering substitute.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains a cumulative mathematical/computational sequence, documented self-driving and traffic-management computer-vision applications, robotics, networks, product design and lifecycle assessment; the label avoids claiming automotive mechanics or electronics.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Programming precedes algorithms, networks, planning and reinforcement learning; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Numerical Methods and Linear Systems occur in the sole available fourth semester, while Advanced Calculus follows when next offered.

alternatives.label: Sustainable energy, product systems & intelligent mobility
alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical modelling, perception, robotics and intelligent decisions while adding lifecycle assessment, renewable-energy design, climate context and material recovery for lower-impact mobility and product systems.
alternatives.labelReason: Five sustainability courses provide a cumulative lifecycle, energy and resource strand alongside quantitative intelligent-system methods; the label does not imply battery, power-electronics or vehicle-design engineering.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes Renewable System Design and resource recovery. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede their dependent advanced courses. Advanced Calculus follows Numerical Methods and Linear Systems because its next exact offering is the final spring.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ: discrete logic, databases, networks, advanced algorithms and AI ethics are replaced by two sustainability foundations, climate change, renewable-system design and resource recovery. These changes implement the evidenced low-impact electric-mobility direction.

candidates.label: Sustainable electric mobility and product systems
Vehicle mechanics, propulsion and electromechanical integration

selection.assessment: Two related-fields responses pass the academic and mechanical gates and differ by five courses / 37.5 EC. A further vehicle-mechanics and propulsion direction cannot supply mechanics, thermodynamics, road-vehicle dynamics, circuits, electromagnetics, electromechanics, power electronics or powertrain laboratories. General calculus, linear systems, robotics and renewable-energy assessment cannot be relabelled as that physical-engineering formation. The 45 EC of genuine external free choice remains open and is not used to manufacture another target route.

notes.text: Automotive Technology integrates mechanics, electronics, electromechanics, power conversion, embedded hardware, vehicle networks, propulsion, road-vehicle dynamics, laboratories and an automotive final project. The UCR curricula support computational autonomous systems or sustainable energy/product systems related to mobility; they do not reproduce that complete vehicle-engineering formation.
